what_its_for: Darifenacin is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, frequent trips to the bathroom, and accidental leakage of urine (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or split the tablet, as it is designed to release the medicine slowly over time. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is one 7.5 mg tablet once daily. After 2 weeks, your doctor may increase your dose to one 15 mg tablet once daily if needed. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for the missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice while taking this medication, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise the risk of side effects. Avoid activities that require you to be fully alert, such as driving or operating heavy machinery, until you know how this medication affects you, as it may cause blurred vision or dizziness. Be careful in hot weather or during exercise, as this medication can reduce sweating and increase the risk of overheating. Limit alcohol, as it can worsen dizziness and drowsiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: inability to urinate or difficulty emptying your bladder, severe constipation or stomach pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, confusion or memory problems, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, or severe eye pain or sudden vision changes (which could be signs of a rare eye condition called angle-closure glaucoma). Also call your doctor if side effects like dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, or dizziness are bothering you or not going away.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice some improvement in your bladder symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking this medication. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): You may be more sensitive to side effects like confusion, dizziness, and constipation. Use with caution and report any new or worsening symptoms to your doctor. Liver problems: If you have moderate liver disease, your doctor will likely keep your dose at 7.5 mg and not increase it. This medication is NOT recommended if you have severe liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if this medication is safe during pregnancy or if it passes into breast milk. Children: This medication is not approved for use in children.
